note: Written predictions are published ONLY for HIGH-confidence picks. Every factual claim below is traceable to an official source listed in 'sources'; the only opinion is the selection itself. Comparative claims were checked against the official table before publishing.

predictions.headline: Zebre's leaking defence points to a home win for Connacht in Galway
predictions.body: Selection: Connacht to win the match. Connacht sit 14th in the United Rugby Championship on 5 points after three rounds, but they now meet the one side below them at Dexcom Stadium. Zebre Parma are 16th and winless, with 116 points conceded in three matches - an average of 38.7 per game - and they lost 12-29 at home to Edinburgh in Round 3. Connacht went down 36-19 at Glasgow on 9 October, so they will be keen to bank a win here. Zebre have conceded 17 tries in three games, and that trend, rather than anything Connacht have shown so far, is what makes the home side the call. Our price is short, so the handicap is the better way in.

predictions.selection: Vodacom Bulls to win (3-way match betting)
predictions.headline: Loftus form guide: the Bulls' 126 points in three games meets a winless Ulster
predictions.body: Selection: Bulls to win. The Bulls have scored 126 points across three rounds - 42 per game - and hold the best points differential in the competition at +72, after beating the Lions 57-15 at Loftus Versfeld on 10 October. Ulster arrive 11th with no wins from three, having drawn 26-26 with Munster at the Affidea Stadium in Round 3 after drawing the round before. Ulster have scored 88 points in three games, so they are not toothless, but they have not yet closed out an 80-minute performance. An early kick-off at Loftus Versfeld, against a pack that has conceded only seven tries, is a hard place to find a first win.

predictions.selection: DHL Stormers to win (3-way match betting)
predictions.headline: Stormers' defensive record should hold up against a Scarlets side still finding its feet
predictions.body: Selection: Stormers to win. The Stormers are fourth on 11 points with a +27 differential, built on 54 points conceded in three matches, and they beat the Sharks 39-22 at DHL Stadium on 10 October - the same venue as this fixture. Scarlets are 12th on 7 points and have conceded 85, most recently edging Benetton 27-26 in Round 3, a match decided by a single point. Scarlets have lost two of three and now travel to a side that has conceded the joint-fewest points in the league. With the Stormers' forward carries and lineout drive working, the hosts should be able to keep Scarlets at arm's length and cover a moderate handicap.

predictions.headline: Leinster's 29-5 dismantling of Cardiff is the form line that matters at the Aviva
predictions.body: Selection: Leinster to win. Leinster are only 10th on 8 points after an uncharacteristically slow start - one win from three - but that win was a 29-5 demolition of Cardiff in Round 3 in which they conceded a single try. Munster are a place higher on 9 points after drawing 26-26 at Ulster, and they have scored 72 points while conceding 74. Leinster have the fourth-fewest points conceded in the league (58) and face a Munster side that has won once in three. At the Aviva Stadium, with a defence that has given up eight tries in three matches, Leinster look the more solid side; take the outright market rather than a tight handicap.

predictions.selection: Buffalo Sabres money line (2-way, overtime included)
predictions.headline: Flyers' 0-4-1 road record makes Buffalo the call at KeyBank Center
predictions.body: Selection: Sabres money line. Buffalo are 4-3-2 for 10 points and have been respectable at home at 3-2-0, scoring 27 goals across nine games while conceding 34. Philadelphia are the story here for the wrong reasons: 2-6-3 with 17 goals in 11 games, the lowest goals-per-game rate of any Eastern Conference team in the NHL.com standings, and a road record of 0-4-1. The Flyers have won their last two games, which is why this is not a bigger price, but both wins came with home ice. Buffalo's home form against a Philadelphia side that has not won on the road all season makes the Sabres the side to be on; the puck line is a step too far given Buffalo's own defensive numbers.
